items.title: Coast Guard closes three-mile Mississippi River section after New Orleans tanker collision
items.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard halted vessel traffic between Mississippi River mile markers 93 and 96 after the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans. This is a verified disruption to a major shipping corridor, but no petroleum export losses, refinery outage or commodity-price impact has been established. Reopening and vessel queues determine commercial significance.

observations.label: Incident November 13
observations.value: Approximately 12:30 PM Central (1:30 PM EST); tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with docked American Heritage river cruise vessel in New Orleans.

observations.label: Verified physical-flow restriction
observations.value: Coast Guard reported Mississippi River closed to vessel traffic at mile marker 96; reporting identifies restricted area between river miles 93 and 96.

observations.label: Market impact assessment
observations.value: No verified crude or petroleum-product export curtailment, refinery shutdown, cargo loss or price move attributable to the collision at research cutoff.

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Coast Guard reopening and safety notices; downstream and upstream vessel queues; petrochemical and oil-product barge delays. Rapid reopening with no cargo delays would limit market effect.

items.key_finding: A confirmed three-mile Mississippi River closure creates a physical maritime bottleneck, with energy-market consequences unquantified.

sources.title: Navy Times: Coast Guard confirms Mississippi River traffic closure, November 13
Associated Press: tanker collision at New Orleans, November 13
Guardian: three-mile river closure reported, November 13

items.title: Nebius AI-cloud shares slide as capacity delays collide with $40B-$45B 2027 capex plan
items.summary: Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%, but expects 2026 sales near the low end of guidance because some data-center capacity is delayed into 2027. Its planned 2027 investment of $40 billion-$45 billion highlights funding and execution risk despite customer demand. The intraday decline extends pressure on debt-dependent AI infrastructure providers.

observations.label: Reuters November 13 report updated 12:18 PM EST
observations.value: NBIS -9.0%; CRWV -8.8% intraday in Reuters snapshot; not closing prices

observations.label: Nebius Q3 2026 results reported November 12
observations.value: Revenue $980.8M, +571% year-over-year; adjusted EBITDA $465.8M; net loss from continuing operations $37.5M

observations.label: 2026 guidance revision
observations.value: Now expects revenue at low end of prior $3.0B-$3.4B range due to deferred third-party data-center capacity

observations.label: 2027 construction funding
observations.value: Preliminary 2027 capex $40B-$45B; 2027 revenue outlook $12B-$13B; management says prepayments and contract-backed financing are expected to cover 75%-85% of spending

observations.label: Watch and invalidation
observations.value: Vineland/New Jersey power readiness, capacity activation, customer contract conversion, interest and debt costs, 2027 funding sources. On-time delivery and falling financing costs would weaken the bearish read

items.key_finding: Explosive AI-cloud revenue growth is not insulating Nebius from power-delivery timing and enormous financing demands.

sources.title: Reuters, Neoclouds and AI stocks slide November 13
WSJ, Nebius outlook and funding for AI buildout November 12

items.title: Liftoff Mobile jumps on profitable growth and raised guidance
items.summary: Liftoff Mobile shares rose roughly 25% in Friday trading after third-quarter revenue increased 32% and adjusted EBITDA rose 45%. Management raised its full-year revenue forecast as its Cortex ad platform improved monetization. Strong free cash flow supports the fundamentals, but rising expectations and advertising cyclicality remain risks.

observations.label: November 13 Friday market observation
observations.value: LFTO approximately +25%, reported by Barron's in Friday stock-movers coverage; indicative intraday, not a closing price.

observations.label: Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue
observations.value: $237.5 million, +32% year over year; company earnings release Nov. 12.

observations.label: Q3 adjusted EBITDA and net income
observations.value: Adjusted EBITDA $144.9 million, +45%; net income approximately $86.7 million; company filing.

observations.label: 2026 revenue guidance
observations.value: Raised to $907-$912 million; adjusted EBITDA $547-$551 million.

observations.label: Cash-generation context
observations.value: Trailing 12-month free cash flow $249 million, company-defined non-GAAP.

observations.label: Risks, next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Watch advertiser spending and customer ROI, daily average revenue, Q4 results, EBITDA quality, and share-price follow-through; loss of customer growth would weaken the thesis.

items.key_finding: Profitable AI advertising software growth produced an outsized positive equity response amid broad tech weakness.

sources.title: Liftoff investor relations Q3 2026 results, Nov 12

items.title: AI semiconductor selloff broadens across AMD, Broadcom and Nvidia
items.summary: Late-morning reporting shows AMD down about 10.2%, Broadcom down 6.5% and Nvidia down 4.2%, with the Nasdaq down 1.9%. Investors are reassessing AI infrastructure returns amid Nvidia leadership uncertainty and higher borrowing costs. These are intraday observations, not closing prices.

observations.label: Late morning November 13, intraday
observations.value: AMD -10.2%; AVGO -6.5%; NVDA -4.2%; Nasdaq -1.9%, AP

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Semiconductor breadth, volume, Treasury yields, AI capex guidance; broad sustained rebound would weaken the signal

items.key_finding: Chip weakness has broadened from Nvidia to major AI semiconductor peers.

items.title: IEA finds crude supply recovery alongside persistent diesel and tanker stress
items.summary: The IEA reports October global oil supply rose to 105.4 million barrels daily and inventories increased by 52 million barrels. Gulf exports recovered despite attacks, but onshore stocks remain unusually low, diesel near $180 per barrel in Europe and Middle East-to-Asia freight near records. This is evidence of recovering crude flows, not an end to physical shipping risk.

observations.label: October global supply
observations.value: 105.4 million barrels/day, up 2.3 million barrels/day month on month (IEA)

observations.label: October inventories
observations.value: +52 million barrels observed; onshore inventories lowest since at least 2016

observations.label: Gulf exports excluding Oman
observations.value: 18.4 million barrels/day, 26% below pre-war level

observations.label: Diesel and freight
observations.value: European diesel near $180/barrel, 77% above pre-war; Middle East-to-Asia crude tanker rates near records

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO/MARAD, verified transit and export volumes, diesel cracks, freight premiums and OPEC/IEA revisions; renewed export losses would undermine rebalancing

items.key_finding: Crude recovery is measurable, while diesel and tanker bottlenecks remain material.
